soru_metni: (I) El Niño is a climate pattern characterized by the unusual warming of surface waters in the Pacific Ocean. (II) This phenomenon occurs every few years, disrupting typical global weather patterns significantly. (III) It can lead to severe droughts in Australia and heavy rainfall and flooding in South America. (IV) Ocean shipping routes are carefully planned by logistics companies to avoid tropical storms. (V) Understanding El Niño is crucial for meteorologists to predict and prepare for extreme global weather events. Seçenekler:
aciklama: Paragraf El Niño iklim olayının Pasifik'teki oluşumu, küresel hava durumuna etkileri ve tahmin edilmesinin önemini konu edinmektedir. IV. cümle ise meteorolojik olaydan sapıp nakliye şirketlerinin okyanus rotalarını fırtınalara göre planlamasından bahsetmektedir.

soru_metni: (I) Gothic architecture is a historical style of building that flourished in Europe during the High Middle Ages. (II) It is characterized by stained-glass windows, pointed arches, and flying buttresses. (III) These features allowed builders to construct much taller cathedrals with abundant interior natural light. (IV) Castle walls in the Middle Ages were built thick and windowless primarily for defense purposes. (V) Famous examples of this grandiose style include the Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris. Seçenekler:

(II) Studies show that being bilingual enhances cognitive flexibility and improves problem-solving skills in children. (III) Learning a foreign language vocabulary requires consistent memorization and practice over time. (IV) It can also delay the onset of age-related cognitive decline, such as Alzheimer's, in older adults. soru_metni: (I) Virtual reality, or VR, is an artificial computer-generated environment that simulates a realistic experience. (II) Users wear a specialized headset that tracks their head movements, creating an immersive 3D world. (III) Computer monitors have become much thinner and lighter over the past decade due to LED technology. (IV) Beyond gaming, VR is increasingly used for training medical students and pilots in risk-free simulations. (II) They huddle together in massive, tightly packed groups to share warmth and shield themselves from icy winds. (III) Penguins cannot fly, but they are incredibly agile swimmers underwater when hunting fish. (IV) Individuals rotate from the cold outer edges of the huddle to the warm center continuously. (V) This cooperative behavior is essential for conserving energy and ensuring the survival of the colony. Seçenekler:

III. cümle ise bu toplumsal ısınma mekanizmasını keserek penguenlerin uçamaması ve iyi yüzmesi gibi genel bir fiziksel özelliğe değinmektedir.

soru_metni: (I) The Magna Carta, signed in England in 1215, is one of the most famous documents in world history. (II) It was drafted to limit the absolute power of King John and protect the rights of barons. (III) British museums hold many historical royal crowns made of gold and precious gems. (IV) By stating that even the king was subject to the law, it established the principle of rule of law. (V) This historic document laid the legal foundation for modern democratic governance and constitutional rights. Seçenekler:
aciklama: Paragraf Magna Carta'nın kralın yetkilerini sınırlama amacını, hukuk devleti ilkesini başlatmasını ve demokrasi tarihindeki önemini ele almaktadır. III. cümle ise belgeden saparak İngiliz müzelerindeki kraliyet taçlarının yapım malzemelerinden bahsetmektedir.

soru_metni: (I) Vitamin D is a vital nutrient that plays a crucial role in maintaining strong bones and teeth. (II) It helps the human body absorb calcium from the food we consume daily. (III) Unlike most other vitamins, our body can synthesize vitamin D when skin is exposed to natural sunlight. (IV) Sunscreen protects our skin from harmful ultraviolet radiation that can cause painful sunburns. (V) Consequently, a lack of sunlight exposure can lead to severe bone deficiencies like rickets. (III) When forests are cleared, rain washes away the fertile topsoil, leaving the land dry and barren. (V) This fertile soil is crucial for farming crops like wheat, rice, and corn to feed populations. (V) Over time, this erosion can turn productive farmlands into barren deserts, a process known as desertification. Seçenekler:

soru_metni: (I) The Indo-European language family is the largest in the world, encompassing hundreds of modern languages. (II) It includes major languages like Spanish, English, Hindi, and Russian, which share a common ancestral tongue. (III) Learning to speak multiple languages is highly beneficial for improving brain health in adults. (IV) Linguists discovered this relationship by analyzing shared grammatical structures and vocabularies across these languages. soru_metni: (I) Quantum mechanics is a fundamental theory in physics that describes the nature and behavior of matter at the atomic level. (II) Developed in the early 20th century, it challenged many laws of classical physics established by Isaac Newton. (III) Max Planck and Albert Einstein were among the pioneering scientists who laid its mathematical foundations. (IV) Telescope designs have been upgraded recently to observe distant stellar systems with higher clarity. (V) Today, this theory is essential for explaining how semiconductors, lasers, and modern computers function. Seçenekler:

soru_metni: (I) Urbanization is the historical process where large numbers of people permanently concentrate in relatively small areas, forming cities. (II) This shift is primarily driven by people searching for better job opportunities and modern education. (III) Cities offer advanced healthcare facilities, cultural centers, and extensive public transit networks. (IV) Public transit systems require large financial subsidies from national governments to remain cheap. (V) However, rapid urbanization can also lead to overcrowding, air pollution, and severe housing shortages. Seçenekler:
aciklama: Paragraf kentleşmenin (urbanization) tanımı, nedenleri, sunduğu imkanlar ve yol açtığı sorunları ele almaktadır. IV. cümle ise genel kentleşme ve şehir yaşamı akışından saparak toplu taşıma sistemlerine verilen devlet sübvansiyonlarından bahsetmektedir.

soru_metni: (I) The periodic table is a tabular display of chemical elements organized by their atomic numbers. (II) It was famously formulated by the Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869. (III) Mendeleev is remembered as a passionate educator who wrote several popular chemistry textbooks. (IV) He left gaps in his table to accurately predict the properties of elements that were undiscovered at that time. (V) Today, the periodic table serves as an invaluable reference tool for scientists and students in chemistry. Seçenekler:
aciklama: Paragraf periyodik tablonun organizasyon yapısını, Mendeleev tarafından formüle edilişini ve henüz keşfedilmemiş elementleri tahmin etme başarısını anlatmaktadır. III. cümle ise tablo odaklı akışı keserek Mendeleev'in kişisel öğretmenlik kariyerinden ve yazdığı ders kitaplarından bahsetmektedir.

soru_metni: (I) Emotional intelligence, or EQ, refers to the ability to understand and manage your own emotions and those of others. (II) It consists of key skills such as empathy, self-awareness, motivation, and social skills. (III) Studies show that leaders with high EQ are much better at motivating teams and resolving office conflicts. (IV) Standard IQ tests are typically used by schools to measure academic intelligence and logical reasoning. (V) Unlike IQ, emotional intelligence is not fixed and can be developed throughout a person's life. Seçenekler:
aciklama: Paragraf duygusal zekanın (EQ) tanımı, bileşenleri, iş hayatındaki önemi ve geliştirilebilir olmasını anlatmaktadır. IV. cümle ise duygusal zeka akışını keserek akademik zekayı ölçen standart IQ testlerinin okulda kullanımından bahsetmektedir.

soru_metni: (I) Cloud computing allows users to store and access data over the internet instead of on a local hard drive. (II) This technology enables businesses to reduce IT costs by outsourcing physical server maintenance. (III) Hard drives utilize spinning magnetic disks to write and read digital information. (V) Consequently, cloud services have become essential for supporting remote work models globally. Seçenekler:

(III) Roman emperors frequently wore expensive purple robes made of imported silk to show their power. (IV) Merchants traveled in caravans for protection against bandits and harsh weather in central Asian deserts. soru_metni: (I) Mitosis is a fundamental biological process of cell division that results in two identical daughter cells. (II) It is crucial for growth, tissue repair, and asexual reproduction in multicellular organisms. (III) During this process, the cell's genetic material is duplicated and distributed equally between the new cells. (IV) Cancer cells divide uncontrollably, forming tumors that can invade and damage healthy body tissues. (V) This precise division ensures that every new cell possesses a complete copy of the organism's DNA. Seçenekler:
aciklama: Paragraf mitoz bölünmenin tanımı, büyüme/onarımdaki işlevi ve hücre içindeki genetik materyalin eşit dağılım sürecini açıklamaktadır. IV. cümle ise normal mitoz bölünme sürecinden saparak kanser hücrelerinin kontrolsüz bölünmesini ve tümör oluşturmasını anlatmaktadır.

soru_metni: (I) The greenhouse effect is a natural process that warms the Earth's surface to temperatures suitable for life. (II) Greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide and water vapor trap heat from the Sun in our atmosphere. (III) Planting trees is an effective way to absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere through photosynthesis. (IV) Without this natural warming mechanism, the Earth would be frozen and uninhabitable for humans. (V) However, human activities are currently enhancing this effect, leading to global warming. III. cümle ise sera etkisi sürecinden saparak fotosentez yoluyla ağaç dikmenin karbon emilimi üzerindeki genel faydasına değinmektedir.

(II) Impressionist painters rejected traditional studio techniques in favor of painting outdoors in natural light. (III) It is generated through a chemical reaction involving a light-emitting pigment called luciferin. (II) In the late 20th century, scientists discovered that chemicals like chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) were depleting this protective layer. (III) This discovery led to the 1987 Montreal Protocol, an international treaty designed to phase out these ozone-depleting substances. (IV) Sunscreen lotions are highly recommended by dermatologists to protect the skin from painful sunburns. (V) Thanks to this global cooperation, the ozone layer is slowly recovering and is expected to heal completely in the coming decades. Seçenekler:

(II) In a hydroponic system, plant roots receive essential minerals directly from the water, which accelerates their growth. (III) Organic compost can be made easily at home by recycling organic kitchen waste like fruit peels. (IV) Because it does not require soil, this technique can be used in urban environments or barren regions where farming is impossible. (V) Additionally, hydroponic farming uses up to ninety percent less water than traditional soil-based agriculture, making it highly sustainable. Seçenekler:

(II) It aimed to collect the world's knowledge, housing hundreds of thousands of papyrus scrolls containing works of philosophy, science, and literature. (III) Scholars from all over the Mediterranean world traveled to this institution to study and conduct research. (IV) Modern public libraries often provide free high-speed internet access and digital book downloads for their members. (II) To echolocate, bats emit high-frequency sound waves that bounce off nearby obstacles and prey. (III) By analyzing the returning echoes, they can determine the precise size, distance, and speed of insects. (IV) City councils are implementing new laws to protect endangered bat species living in urban buildings. (V) This highly precise mechanism allows bats to navigate complex forest structures easily without relying on eyesight. Seçenekler:

soru_metni: (I) The Apollo 11 mission in July 1903 marked a monumental milestone in human history as astronauts landed on the Moon for the first time. (III) The entire event was broadcast live to millions of viewers worldwide, showcasing human technological capability. soru_metni: (I) Dark matter is a mysterious, invisible form of matter that makes up about eighty-five percent of the matter in the universe. (II) Unlike regular matter, it does not emit, absorb, or reflect light, making it completely undetectable by traditional telescopes. (III) Scientists can only observe dark matter indirectly through its gravitational pull on visible stars and galaxies. (IV) Telescope lenses must be cleaned carefully with special chemicals to prevent scratching the delicate glass. (V) Understanding this unseen force is crucial, as it acts as a cosmic cement holding galaxies together. Seçenekler:

soru_metni: (I) The placebo effect is a fascinating psychological phenomenon where patients experience genuine medical improvements after receiving inactive treatments. (II) This improvement occurs because the patient strongly believes that the fake medicine is a real, effective drug. (III) Brain scans show that expecting a treatment to work can trigger the release of natural pain-killing chemicals. (IV) Regulatory agencies often delay the approval of new drugs due to lengthy safety testing procedures. (V) Consequently, clinical trials must utilize a placebo group to accurately measure the true effectiveness of new medications. Seçenekler:

soru_metni: (I) The Vikings were skilled Norse seafarers and traders who explored and settled in parts of Europe between the 8th and 11th centuries. (II) They designed unique longships that were fast, lightweight, and capable of navigating both shallow rivers and open oceans. (III) These advanced ships allowed them to conduct sudden raids and establish profitable trade networks across vast distances. (IV) Many families today prefer skiing holidays in modern Scandinavian resorts during the winter. (V) Beyond raiding, their extensive voyages led to the colonization of Iceland, Greenland, and even parts of North America. Seçenekler:

soru_metni: (I) Acid rain is a harmful environmental issue caused by sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides released into the atmosphere by factories. (II) These gases react with water molecules in clouds to form mild acids that fall to the ground with rain or snow. (III) Acid rain damages forests by washing away essential nutrients from the soil and harming tree leaves. (IV) Tree-planting volunteers often organize weekend trips to restore eroded forest areas. (V) Additionally, it increases the acidity of lakes and rivers, making them toxic to fish and other aquatic organisms. Seçenekler:

soru_metni: (I) Hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used by ancient Egyptians to record their history, laws, and religious beliefs. (II) This system combined logographic, syllabic, and alphabetic elements, utilizing hundreds of detailed pictures and symbols. (III) Scribes spent many years learning this complex system, as writing was a highly prestigious profession in Egypt. (IV) The papyrus plant was harvested along the Nile River to manufacture ancient paper scrolls. (V) These hieroglyphic inscriptions were carved on temple walls and painted on tombs to preserve royal achievements. Seçenekler:

soru_metni: (I) Nanotechnology involves the study and manipulation of matter at an incredibly small scale, typically between 1 and 100 nanometers. (II) At this level, materials display unique physical and chemical properties that differ from their larger forms. (III) Engineers use these tiny structures to create lighter, stronger materials and faster computer processors. (IV) Python and Java are currently two of the most popular programming languages for software development. (V) In medicine, nanotechnology is being developed to deliver drugs directly to cancer cells with extreme precision. Seçenekler:

soru_metni: (I) The Byzantine Empire was the continuation of the Roman Empire in its eastern provinces during Late Antiquity and the Middle Ages. (II) With its capital in Constantinople, it survived for over a thousand years after the collapse of the Western Roman Empire. (III) The empire developed a rich cultural blend of Roman law, Greek culture, and Christian theology. (IV) Real estate prices in modern Istanbul have risen significantly due to foreign investments. (V) Despite constant threats from invaders, Constantinople remained a major trade hub and cultural capital of the medieval world. Seçenekler:

(II) They are often referred to as "friendly bacteria" because they help maintain a healthy balance of microorganisms in your gut. (III) Probiotics can help restore this natural balance, particularly after it has been disrupted by taking antibiotics. (IV) Dairy farms must use pasteurization techniques to heat milk and kill harmful bacteria before bottling. (II) It is characterized by wedge-shaped marks pressed into soft clay tablets using a stylus made of a reed. (III) Clay pottery classes have become a popular therapeutic hobby for adults in modern cities. (IV) Originally used for keeping trade records and inventories, it slowly evolved to record literature and laws. (V) This historic writing system allowed Mesopotamian civilizations to preserve their culture and history across millennia. Seçenekler:

(III) This vapor condenses into clouds and eventually falls back to the ground as precipitation, such as rain or snow. soru_metni: (I) The nitrogen cycle is a vital biogeochemical process that converts nitrogen in the atmosphere into usable forms for living things. (II) Although nitrogen makes up most of our atmosphere, plants cannot absorb it directly in its gaseous form. (III) Soil bacteria play a key role by fixing nitrogen gas into nitrates that plants can absorb through their roots. (IV) Liquid nitrogen is widely used in laboratories and industries to freeze biological samples rapidly. (V) This constant recycling ensures that ecosystems receive a continuous supply of this essential element. Seçenekler:

(II) When a material becomes a superconductor, it can also repel magnetic fields, allowing for magnetic levitation. (III) Copper wires are still widely used in domestic grids to deliver electrical power to homes. (IV) This unique property could revolutionize power grids by preventing the massive energy loss that occurs during transmission. (V) Today, superconductivity is utilized in advanced technologies like MRI scanners and high-speed maglev trains. Seçenekler:
aciklama: Paragraf süperiletkenlik olgusunu, manyetik itme kuvvetini ve bu teknolojinin MRI ve Maglev trenlerindeki modern uygulamalarını ele almaktadır. III. cümle ise süperiletkenlikten tamamen uzaklaşarak evsel şebekelerdeki standart bakır kablo kullanımına değinmektedir.

(II) Housed in the Louvre Museum in Paris, it is celebrated for the subject's subtle, mysterious smile and the soft blending technique known as sfumato. (III) Art restoration projects require chemists to analyze paint pigments carefully to avoid damaging ancient layers. (II) This temperature difference is caused by buildings and concrete roads, which absorb and trap heat from the Sun. (III) Cities also lack trees and green spaces that would otherwise provide cooling shade and moisture through evaporation. (IV) City councils are increasing parking fines to discourage drivers from bringing cars into downtown areas. (II) Maya astronomers made highly precise observations of the movements of stars and planets, particularly Venus. (III) They developed a solar calendar containing 365 days, showcasing their remarkable scientific sophistication. (II) Its primary function is to transport lymph, a clear fluid containing white blood cells that fight harmful infections. (III) Lymph nodes act as tiny filters, trapping and destroying dangerous bacteria, viruses, and foreign particles. (IV) Many herbal detox teas are sold online with promises of flushing out toxic substances from the body rapidly. (V) By filtering this fluid, the system plays a critical role in protecting the body against diseases and maintaining fluid balance. Seçenekler:

(III) They fought in massive structures like the Colosseum, showcasing martial arts before thousands of roaring spectators. (IV) Hollywood movie productions in Rome spent millions of dollars recreating ancient monuments for historical films. (V) Although their fights were dangerous and often deadly, successful gladiators could gain immense fame and even their freedom. Seçenekler:

soru_metni: (I) E-waste, or electronic waste, is a rapidly growing environmental concern caused by discarded devices like smartphones and computers. (III) When e-waste is burned in open areas, it releases dangerous chemical fumes that threaten the health of local communities. (V) Lithium batteries used in electric cars require rare minerals mined under strict environmental regulations. (V) Developing recycling facilities is crucial for recovering valuable metals from these devices safely. Seçenekler:
aciklama: Paragraf elektronik atıkların (e-waste) çevre ve insan sağlığına verdiği zararları ve geri dönüşümün önemini anlatmaktadır. IV. cümle ise bu atık krizinden saparak elektrikli arabalarda kullanılan lityum pillerin madencilik kurallarına odaklanmaktadır.

soru_metni: (I) Papyrus was the primary writing material used in ancient Mediterranean civilizations, particularly in Egypt. (II) It was manufactured from the stem of the papyrus plant, a tall reed that grew abundantly along the banks of the Nile River. (III) Scribes peeled the stems, cut them into thin strips, and pressed them together to form flat, durable sheets. (IV) Modern reed boats are designed by adventurers to sail across oceans and test ancient migration routes. (V) These papyrus scrolls allowed ancient Egyptians to record their government archives, religious texts, and literature. Seçenekler:
aciklama: Paragraf papirüs kâğıdının tarihini, Nil kıyısında yetişen sazlıklardan nasıl üretildiğini ve tarihi kayıtlardaki rolünü ele almaktadır. IV. cümle ise papirüs üretimi akışını keserek modern saz tekneleriyle yapılan okyanus seyahatlerinden bahsetmektedir.

soru_metni: (I) Desalination is the industrial process of removing dissolved salts and minerals from seawater to produce fresh drinking water. (II) This technology has become essential for arid regions, such as the Middle East, where freshwater resources are extremely scarce. (III) Most desalination plants utilize thermal distillation or membrane filtration like reverse osmosis. (IV) Sea salt is a popular seasoning prized by chefs for its unique mineral taste and texture. (V) However, the process is highly energy-intensive and produces large amounts of salty wastewater, posing environmental challenges. Seçenekler:
aciklama: Paragraf tuzsuzlaştırma (desalination) teknolojisini, bu teknolojinin kurak bölgelerdeki önemini ve taşıdığı çevresel riskleri anlatmaktadır. IV. cümle ise bu arıtma teknolojisinden tamamen saparak şeflerin tercih ettiği deniz tuzunun tadından ve yapısından bahsetmektedir.

(II) To echolocate, bats emit high-frequency sound waves that bounce off nearby obstacles and prey. (III) By analyzing the returning echoes, they can determine the precise size, distance, and speed of flying insects. (II) These gases react with water molecules in clouds to form mild acids that fall to the ground with rain or snow. (III) Acid rain damages forests by washing away essential nutrients from the soil and harming tree leaves. (IV) Tree-planting volunteers often organize weekend trips to restore eroded forest areas. soru_metni: (I) The Doppler effect is the change in the observed frequency of a wave when the source and the observer are moving. (II) For example, as an ambulance with a siren approaches you, the sound pitch gets higher, and then drops as it moves away. (III) This physical wave shift is also utilized by astronomers to determine whether distant galaxies are moving away from Earth. (IV) Car manufacturers are upgrading built-in radar detectors to help drivers avoid speeding fines on highways. (V) This simple principle of wave physics is crucial for both acoustic studies and modern astrophysics. Seçenekler:

(III) The laws were carved onto a massive, black stone monument and placed in public for all citizens to see. soru_metni: (I) The Coriolis effect is the apparent deflection of moving objects, such as winds, caused by the rotation of the Earth. (II) Because the Earth spins, winds are deflected to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere. (III) This atmospheric deflection plays a major role in dictating global wind patterns and cyclonic storm rotations. (IV) Modern aircraft fuel tanks are designed to store fuel safely inside the wings to optimize weight. (V) Understanding this planetary force is essential for meteorologists to model and predict weather patterns accurately. Seçenekler:

(II) This mechanism ensures that cellular activities can occur efficiently, even when external temperatures fluctuate. (III) For example, humans sweat to cool down their skin and shiver to generate internal metabolic heat. (IV) Electric blankets are highly popular during winter months because they help people sleep comfortably in cold rooms. III. cümle ise tablo odaklı akışı keserek Mendeleev'in kişisel öğretmenlik kariyerinden ve yazdığı ders kitaplarından bahsetmektedir.

(IV) Standard IQ tests are typically used by schools to measure academic intelligence and logical reasoning.
